title: AI Ethics
intro: Amid concerns about AI-enabled cyber threats, chip access and the ethics of powerful institutions, these stories ask how AI could serve humanity—not simply automate human-centered work. Could stronger ethical guidance and public accountability help keep increasingly capable systems aligned with human values?

items.title: Can ethical traditions help guide AI alignment?
items.description: Anthropic consulted Vedanta monk Swami Sarvapriyananda and other contributors on AI ethics, consciousness and alignment. Their discussion raises questions about whether values and ethical frameworks can help guide increasingly capable AI beyond simple rule-following.

items.title: Japan weighs penalties to strengthen its AI law
items.description: Japan is considering penalties for AI companies that refuse government orders or fail to cooperate with investigations. The proposal could add enforcement tools to a law that currently relies largely on investigation and guidance; the details are still under review.

items.title: U.S. moves to restrict remote access to advanced AI chips
items.description: The Associated Press reports that new U.S. rules target remote access to advanced computing chips and servers, aiming to limit indirect access to powerful AI hardware. The move raises questions about how governments balance national security, chip access and the global development of AI.

items.title: Where are the guardrails for AI?
items.description: Published in February 2020—more than six years ago—Gary A. Bolles' argument for transparent, enforceable AI guardrails still resonates as governments and companies debate alignment, oversight and accountability. The article asks whether AI needs safeguards comparable in purpose, if not form, to Sarbanes-Oxley.

items.title: A weekend trip to see Starship Flight 15
items.description: Published Nov. 16, this first-person account recounts a Nov. 13–14 trip to South Padre Island to watch Starship Flight 15: the booster catch failed, the ship was caught successfully, and the mission deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The curator describes the trip as powered by Grok; the post's source note separately credits Claude, real photos and Wikipedia.
